title.en: Geography: Physical Geography of Tamil Nadu

text.en: Meena looked at the map of Tamil Nadu. "Hills, plains and a long coast," she said.

Tamil Nadu lies in the south-east of India, bordered by the Bay of Bengal and the Indian Ocean. Its relief includes the Western Ghats in the west, the Eastern Ghats and plateau regions, the central plains and the Coromandel coastal plain.
The major rivers are the Cauvery, Vaigai, Tamirabarani, Palar and Pennaiyar. The Cauvery delta has extensive alluvial soils and supports important rice-growing areas. Tamil Nadu's soils are red, black, alluvial and laterite.
The climate is generally tropical, with marked differences between higher hills and lower plains. Both monsoons bring rain, but the northeast monsoon is especially important along much of the coast. Forests are found on the hills, and the Nilgiri Biosphere Reserve, Mudumalai and Anamalai protect wildlife. Palk Bay and the Gulf of Mannar are coastal waters with distinct marine habitats.

text.en: Tamil Nadu generally has a tropical climate, with cooler conditions at higher elevations. The southwest and northeast monsoons contribute rain at different times and places.

text.en: Forests are found on the hills, and the Nilgiri Biosphere Reserve, Mudumalai and Anamalai protect wildlife.

board.text: Coromandel Coast

text.en: Palk Bay lies off the southeast coast. Farther south, the Gulf of Mannar has coastal and marine habitats, including islands, seagrass beds and coral reefs.

board.text: Cauvery

text.en: Tamil Nadu has land neighbours to its north and west and a long coastline to its east and south. The coastline connects several different coastal environments.

board.text: Tamil Nadu occupies the southeastern peninsula

text.en: The Bay of Bengal lies east of much of the state. Farther south, Palk Bay and the Gulf of Mannar are beside the southeastern coast.

board.text: Locate the Bay of Bengal first

text.en: High ground dominates parts of the west. Much of the interior is lower, and the coast includes flat plains and river mouths.

board.text: Relief shifts from mountains to coastal plains

text.en: The Western Ghats form a prominent highland belt. The Nilgiris and Anamalai hills are important parts of the state’s mountain geography.

board.text: Western Ghats rise along the western side

text.en: It is a high peak of the Nilgiris. The elevation helps explain why nearby hill locations are cooler than many places on the plains.

board.text: Doddabetta is in the Nilgiris

text.en: In Tamil Nadu the Eastern Ghats include hill groups such as the Javadi and Shevaroy hills. Valleys and lower land separate parts of the range.

board.text: Eastern Ghats occur as separate hill groups

text.en: A plateau can include rolling land and valleys. It differs from a narrow mountain crest even when it lies at considerable elevation.

board.text: Plateaus are raised areas with relatively broad surfaces

text.en: At the coast, rivers meet the sea and can deposit sediment. Coastal plains include deltas, beaches and other features.

board.text: The Coromandel Coast lies on the east

text.en: Water generally moves from higher ground to lower ground. Hills divide neighbouring drainage basins.

board.text: Drainage follows the slope of the land

text.en: The river enters Tamil Nadu from Karnataka and reaches the delta in the east. Its branches carry water and sediment towards the coast.

board.text: The Cauvery links upland and coastal landscapes

text.en: River-deposited soils and a supply of irrigation water support rice cultivation in parts of the Cauvery delta. Not all fields have the same conditions.

board.text: Alluvium can support delta farming

text.en: The Vaigai drains part of southern Tamil Nadu. Its flow can change with rainfall, reservoirs and withdrawals.

board.text: The Vaigai flows east through Madurai

text.en: The Tamirabarani rises in the southern Western Ghats and flows eastwards to the sea. Its basin is smaller than the Cauvery basin.

board.text: The Tamirabarani drains the far south

text.en: These rivers drain parts of northern and northeastern Tamil Nadu. Their flows are influenced by seasonal rain and local storage.

board.text: Northern river systems include the Palar and Pennaiyar

text.en: The southwest monsoon brings rain to parts of the state. During the northeast monsoon, winds and weather systems over the Bay bring important rain to much of the east coast.

board.text: Two monsoon seasons affect rainfall

text.en: Moist air can drop rain over hills. Drier conditions can occur on the sheltered side, and mountain temperatures are generally lower than at sea level.

board.text: Hills influence rain and temperature

text.en: Weather systems from the Bay of Bengal can bring intense rainfall to some districts. Their effects depend on where they move and how the land drains.

board.text: Coastal storms can bring rain and flooding

text.en: Soils differ because rock, rainfall and the movement of sediment differ across places. A soil map can help explain farming patterns.

board.text: Red, black, alluvial and laterite soils reflect different origins

text.en: Rivers deposit alluvium in many valleys and deltas. On hills, weathered rock and repeated rainfall can produce different soil properties.

board.text: Soils near rivers can differ from soils on hills

text.en: Wetter hills can support forests, and drier areas can support scrub. Coastal wetlands and seagrass beds contain plants adapted to their own conditions.

board.text: Habitats vary across the state

text.en: The Nilgiri Biosphere Reserve includes highland habitats. The Gulf of Mannar Biosphere Reserve includes coastal and marine habitats.

board.text: Protected areas help conserve different ecosystems

text.en: Highlands shape where water flows. Rain supplies the rivers, and low-lying delta land receives some of their sediment. Use these links to explain regional differences.

board.text: Connect relief, rainfall and drainage

problem.en: Why is the Cauvery delta fertile?

text.en: The river brings silt.
The soil is alluvial.
It has water for farming.

problem.en: Why can a hill town in the Nilgiris be cooler than a nearby lowland town?

text.en: Compare their elevations.

why.en: The towns can lie close together and receive similar angles of sunlight.

text.en: Air is generally cooler at higher elevations.

why.en: Relief helps explain a local climate contrast.

problem.en: Why does the Cauvery delta support much rice cultivation?

text.en: The river deposits sediment in its lower course.

why.en: That sediment forms alluvial soils in many delta areas.

text.en: Irrigation and the local growing conditions also matter.

why.en: Soil alone does not explain the full farming pattern.

problem.en: Why does coastal Tamil Nadu often receive substantial rain late in the year?

text.en: The northeast monsoon affects the southeast coast in October to December.

why.en: Moist winds and weather systems can reach the coast from the Bay.

text.en: The coast can receive rain after the main southwest monsoon season elsewhere.

why.en: Places can have different rainy seasons.
